315.h: Philomath University is a private multidisciplinary university licensed by the National Universities Commission on 8 April 2021. It began in the 2021/2022 session with two faculties, Management and Social Sciences, and Law, and has since added two more faculties and a second campus.
315.a: The university offers undergraduate programmes in management, the social sciences and law, with newer faculties added as it grows.
315.c: It is located in Abuja. Its city campus in Maitama opened as an additional site alongside the main campus.

316.h: Plateau State University (PLASU) is a public university owned by the Plateau State Government. It was established under Plateau State Law No. 4 of 7 March 2005 and recognised by the National Universities Commission on 29 April 2005 as Nigeria's 66th university and 24th state university. Teaching began in May 2007 with 480 students, but it was suspended that September and the students were transferred to the University of Jos. The university reopened in October 2010, at the start of the 2010/2011 session.
316.a: The university offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes.
316.c: The campus is in Diram village, on the Butura-Tarangol road in Bokkos local government area, about 70 kilometres from Jos, the state capital.

320.h: Rhema University, Aba is a private Christian university founded by Living Word Ministries International, under the leadership of Emma Okorie. The church set up a planning committee for the university in 2004, and it received its licence from the National Universities Commission and admitted its first students in 2009. It describes its mission as combining teaching, research and community service with the spiritual formation of its students.
320.a: The university offers undergraduate programmes and, through its colleges, higher degrees and postgraduate diplomas.
320.c: It is located in Aba, the commercial city of Abia State.

322.h: Salem University is a private Christian university in Lokoja. The National Universities Commission records its establishment in 2007, while the university dates its founding to 2009. Its name comes from the Hebrew word for 'peace', drawing on the story of Melchizedek's blessing in the Book of Genesis.
322.a: The university combines academic study with spiritual formation in five faculties and colleges, plus a Centre for Continuing Education and Entrepreneurial Studies. It offers undergraduate, postgraduate and professional programmes.
322.c: It is located in Lokoja, the capital of Kogi State, and offers on-campus hostel accommodation.

326.h: Sule Lamido University (SLU) is a public university owned by the Jigawa State Government. It was established on 13 May 2013 as Jigawa State University, received its operating licence from the National Universities Commission in July 2013, and began full academic activities in September 2014. A December 2014 law renamed it after Sule Lamido, the governor at the time. It was created to widen access to higher education for people from Jigawa State and to produce skilled, enterprising graduates.
326.c: The campus is 2 kilometres along the Jahun-Kano road in Kafin Hausa, Jigawa State.

330.h: Taraba State University (TSU) is a public university owned by the Taraba State Government. It was established on 24 January 2008 by Law No. 4 of 2008 of the Taraba State House of Assembly, which Governor Danbaba Danfulani Suntai signed on 28 January 2008. Teaching began in the 2008/2009 session with more than 582 students in its School of General and Preliminary Studies, and full-time degree programmes started in 2009/2010 with 476 students in eighteen departments.
330.a: TSU now offers undergraduate, postgraduate and distance-learning programmes in twelve faculties, with several thousand students.
330.c: It is located in Jalingo, the capital of Taraba State.

340.h: The University of Mkar is a private faith-based university founded by the Universal Reformed Christian Church, known in Tiv as Nongu u Kristu u i Ser sha Tar (NKST). The National Universities Commission licensed it on 6 June 2005. Its pioneer vice-chancellor was Nancy Ngunan Agbe, who served from 2005 to 2011, and Professor Zacharys Anger Gundu has been vice-chancellor since 1 September 2021.
340.a: The university offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes and describes its aim as holistic education that puts God at the centre of learning.
340.c: It is located at the foot of the Mkar Hills, in Gboko local government area of Benue State.
